listeningScripts.title: Phone Plan Upgrade
listeningScripts.text: Customer: Hi, I'm interested in upgrading my phone plan. I currently have the basic plan with 2 GB of data. Support: Great! I can definitely help with that. What's your phone number? Customer: It's 416-555-0234. I'm constantly hitting my data limit, especially with streaming videos. Support: I understand. Let me pull up your account. You're right, your basic plan is 2 GB per month at $35. What data usage would work better for you? Customer: Probably something like 10 GB. How much would that be? Support: We have a 10 GB plan at $65 per month. You'd also get unlimited texting and more calling minutes. Would that interest you? Customer: What's the difference in calling minutes from my current plan? Support: Your current plan has 200 minutes; the 10 GB plan has unlimited calling. Plus, there's no contract change required if you cancel later. Customer: Actually, do you have an 8 GB plan? That might be better value. Support: Good question. We do have an 8 GB plan at $55 per month with the same unlimited calling and texting. Customer: Perfect, I'll take that. When does it take effect? Support: I'm activating it right now. Your bill will reflect the change next billing cycle, which is on July 8th. The monthly cost goes from $35 to $55. Customer: That works for me. Thanks.

listeningScripts.title: Neighbourhood Park Chat
listeningScripts.text: David: Hey, nice day, isn't it? Rebecca: Beautiful. Perfect weather for being outside. David: Have you lived in this neighbourhood long? Rebecca: About five years now. And you? David: Just moved here last month. Rebecca: Oh nice. You picked a good time to arrive. The summer's the best season here. David: So I'm hearing. Any recommendations for places to go? Rebecca: There's a great farmer's market on Saturday mornings at the corner of Main and Oak. The coffee shop near there is amazing too. David: Sounds good. I'll have to check it out. Rebecca: You definitely should. They have the best pastries. Oh, and the park just got new playground equipment if you have kids. David: No kids yet, but that's nice to know. Do many families live here? Rebecca: Lots of young families. It's a very friendly community. David: That's what I was hoping for. I'm looking forward to exploring more.

listeningScripts.title: Travel Insurance Information Session
listeningScripts.text: Welcome to our travel insurance information session. Today, I'll explain the coverage options available through our travel agency. We offer three plans: Basic, Standard, and Premium. The Basic plan covers medical emergencies, emergency dental, and evacuation. Cost is seventy-five dollars for two weeks. The Standard plan includes everything in Basic plus trip cancellation coverage, lost luggage reimbursement up to one thousand dollars, and travel delays over twelve hours. Cost is one hundred twenty dollars for two weeks. The Premium plan is our comprehensive option. It adds accidental death coverage, zero deductible for medical claims, and upgrade to two thousand five hundred dollars for lost luggage. Premium costs two hundred twenty dollars for two weeks. All plans exclude claims related to alcohol impairment or pre-existing medical conditions not disclosed. Coverage begins on your departure date and ends upon return. Claims must be filed within ninety days of the incident. You'll receive a confirmation email with your policy documents. For claims, call our toll-free number at 1-800-555-0147. Representatives are available 24/7. Questions about coverage should be directed to our customer service team. Purchase your policy at least seven days before travel.

listeningScripts.title: New Brunswick Fisheries Management Plan
listeningScripts.text: New Brunswick has introduced a comprehensive fisheries management plan aimed at rebuilding declining fish stocks and supporting the province's fishing communities. The plan allocates 67 million dollars over five years to research, enforcement, and sustainable fishing initiatives. Atlantic salmon populations have declined by 48 percent over the past two decades, prompting urgent action. The plan imposes stricter catch limits on cod and halibut in designated zones. Fishing vessel owners participating in conservation programs receive subsidies up to 200,000 dollars for upgrading to eco-friendly equipment. The program mandates trap modifications to reduce unintended marine mammal bycatch by 35 percent. Over 3,200 fishermen and their families depend on this industry in New Brunswick. The province is establishing a new fisheries research center employing 120 marine scientists. Marine Protected Areas will expand to cover an additional 8 percent of provincial waters. The plan aims to achieve sustainable fish stock levels by 2032.

listeningScripts.title: Community Center Renovation Project
listeningScripts.text:
Recreation Director Karen: We're finally moving forward with the community center renovation that was approved last year. The project is budgeted at 6.8 million dollars and should take about 18 months to complete. We plan to add a new fitness center, upgrade the swimming pool, and create additional youth programming spaces. This will significantly improve our facilities.

Community Member Robert: I'm glad to see this moving forward, Karen, but I'm concerned about one thing. During the construction, the center will be partially closed. My kids attend after-school programs here, and I'm worried about where they'll go during the renovation period. Many families in our community rely on these programs for childcare.

Operations Manager Susan: That's a valid concern, Robert. We've actually planned for this. We'll maintain the community room and outdoor spaces throughout the project. We can relocate the after-school programs there during construction, though it will be more crowded. We're also negotiating with the school district to potentially use school facilities as a backup location for some activities.

Youth Program Coordinator Jason: I'm excited about the upgrades, especially the new youth spaces. But Susan, we need to be realistic about the outdoor space. We currently use it for sports and recreation. If we're moving programs there, we'll have limited room for physical activities. Could we consider using a local park for some outdoor programming during construction?

listeningScripts.title: Mental Health Parity in Insurance Coverage
listeningScripts.text: Mental health needs to be treated with the same importance as physical health in our insurance system. We talk about mental health awareness, but when it comes to actual coverage, it's dramatically underfunded. Most insurance plans cover mental health at lower rates than physical health. If you have a broken arm, insurance covers months of physical therapy. If you have depression or anxiety, you get maybe 10 sessions of therapy a year, and psychologist visits might only be 50 percent covered. This creates barriers. Many people avoid treatment because they can't afford it, and their conditions worsen. The economic impact is massive. Mental health issues cost the economy 51 billion dollars annually in Canada through lost productivity, emergency services, and hospitalizations. Yet we invest a fraction of that in prevention and treatment. Here's what frustrates me most: we have effective treatments. Therapy works. Medication helps. But access is limited by insurance coverage. A person struggling with bipolar disorder shouldn't have to choose between therapy and rent. Insurance companies argue coverage limits are necessary for cost control, but that's shortsighted. When people get mental health treatment early, they use fewer emergency services, work more, and contribute to society. The ROI on mental health coverage is actually positive. I'm advocating for mandatory parity—insurance companies should cover mental health at the same level as physical health. This means removing visit limits, lowering copayments, and covering evidence-based treatments. It's not just compassionate; it's economically smart.
